newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS - UBS profits soar 67 pct in first half.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - UBS profits soar 67 pct in first half.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS), the country's biggest bank, said on Tuesday group net profit surged 67.4 percent in the first half of 1997 to a record 1,856 million Swiss francs ($1.2 billion).
UBS said it was optimistic about performance for full 1997, although conditions in the second half might not be as optimal as in the first six months.
"UBS assumes that its group profit for the full year will enable it to achieve its goal of a return on equity of over 12 percent," the group said.
The results were well-received on the Swiss stock exchange, although analysts said they were disappointed by underlying figures including flat trading income and a 20 percent rise in costs.

The UBS bearer shares rose at first, gaining 22 Swiss francs from the prior close to 1,690, and then fell to around 1,625 francs at midday as some investors took profits on what was seen as good news.
The first-half result was at the top end of analysts' forecasts of between nearly 50 percent and 70 percent.
Estimates are similar to higher for Swiss Bank Corp (SBC), due to announce six-month results on August 13, and Credit Suisse Group, due on August 27.
"Consolidated total assets increased by 77.4 billion to 514.7 billion Swiss francs at mid-year," UBS said in a letter to shareholders.

"A major factor behind our good results was the extraordinary robustness of the financial markets over the first six months, but our own structural re-engineering efforts also produced positive effects," UBS said.
UBS has focused its business in four core divisions and also took an extraordinary charge of three billion Swiss francs last year to cover bad loans in economically weak Switzerland.

The shareholder letter was a record 23 pages as UBS gave more details and a breakdown by division ahead of switching to International Accounting Standards (IAS) for the 1997 full-year report, an effort to provide more transparancy for investors.
The division Private Banking and Institutional Asset Management accounted for more than half of the group's six-month net profit, providing 1.0 billion Swiss francs.
"The continued strategic expansion of asset management and private banking activities both in and outside Switzerland is a top priority for UBS," it said.
Corporate and Institutional Finance, another division, posted after-tax profit of 474 million Swiss francs.
Trading, Sales and Risk Management Services saw net profit of 365 million Swiss francs.
Retail Business Switzerland lost 26 million Swiss francs.
Another 43 million Swiss francs in net profit came from other activities that could not be clearly allocated to one division, UBS said.

UBS said one main reason group profits jumped was last year's decision to take a special charge of three billion Swiss francs to settle a mounting problem with Swiss loans gone bad in the country's stubbornly flat economy.
UBS said it had used roughly 800 million Swiss francs from the exceptional charge in the first half, leaving about 2.2 billion Swiss francs available for future allocations.
New provisions in the first half for credit and country risks were down 82 percent to 137 million francs.
"Our provisioning requirements are likely to be higher in the second half of the year, however," UBS told shareholders.
"This is because new provisions charged to earnings in the first half of the year were below statistical projections."
($ = 1.525 Swiss Francs)
